entries.subject: Disc-resolved images or interferometric imaging of WASP-121
entries.finding: The disc is about 0.05 mas across at 263 pc; no image exists. The sphere carries its Gaia color and a model limb.
entries.revisitWhen: A reconstructed image of the star's surface is published.

entries.subject: The spin axis of WASP-121 on the sky
entries.finding: Bourrier et al. (2020) measure the stellar inclination (8.1 degrees if the north pole is visible, a second solution otherwise) and the planet's nearly polar 3D obliquity, but not the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the axis has no sky direction here; the display axis is celestial north.
entries.revisitWhen: The orbit's orientation on the sky is measured, for example by astrometry or interferometry of the planet.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 6,481 K and log g 4.25 (u1 0.352, u2 0.314): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. Gravity: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-121.json: 4.249.
